members.duties: mechanics audit: damage-budget compliance (flat numbers on Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21), prereq shapes (Adept exactly 2, Master exactly 3), cost math (cards 2/4/8), level gates, dice remnants, stale vocabulary, cross-chapter contradictions
consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance
final quality: structure, cross-references, missing content, completeness
presentation: Quarto/Typst render, heading hierarchy, table formatting/overflow, typography, page flow, card layout, reference-sheet usability, em-dash law

payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch00 Front Matter

Chapter under review: ch00 (quarto-book/chapters/00-front-matter.qmd), "Front Matter"
(title page, copyright block, cover-art placeholder, Credits, Dedication), 56 lines.
First chapter of the book; the book's title page and legal notice. First pending
chapter of Wave 2 (all of Wave 1 is reviewed and merged).

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files ONE finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in 00-front-matter.qmd. Mechanics findings state the broken
value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks use the authoritative chapters as
the reference, not this chapter:

  license/OGC = ch23 (23-license.qmd): the book publishes its game mechanics as Open
    Game Content under the Open Game License Version 1.0a. The Open Game Content
    Declaration designates "all game mechanics, rules systems, and procedures described
    in Chapters 1 through 22" and all spell mechanics as OGC that "may only be Used under
    and in terms of" the OGL 1.0a. The Product Identity list claims all proper names,
    artwork, storylines, and class names. Audit the front-matter copyright block for
    consistency with this grant: a blanket "all rights reserved / no reproduction"
    statement that carves out no OGC exception contradicts the ch23 grant.
  classes = ch05: the 9-class roster (Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd, Intellect,
    Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow).
  opening fiction = ch01b: the title is The Last Ember.

Book conventions every lens applies: zero em-dashes in the book, no stale or retired
vocabulary, placeholder content (TBD, [To be assigned]) is ACCEPTABLE in a draft build
and is NOT a defect to fix now (flag only if a placeholder is wrong or inconsistent,
not merely absent). The cover-art image at line 32 (assets/images/page001-img001.png)
is a real, committed placeholder asset with a correct caption; do not flag its presence.
Typography: the copyright symbol, punctuation, and grammar of the fixed prose lines are
in scope; the TBD placeholders are not.

Disposition tiers the final recommendation must use:
  TIER 1 mechanical — chapter-local, no mechanics change, no content judgment
    (typography, punctuation, grammar, single-cell fixes).
  TIER 2 substantive — content rewrites, cross-chapter reconciliation.
  TIER 3 design-decision — legal or design-authority questions for the lead designer
    (e.g. how the copyright block should express the OGC carve-out).
Also flag any finding that is a BOOK-WIDE convention (visible in sibling chapters),
because a chapter-local fix would make ch00 inconsistent with the book; those route to
a convention decision, not a single-chapter edit.

payload.argument: ch00 frames the book's legal face: its blanket no-reproduction notice (00-front-matter.qmd:22) conflicts with ch23's OGC grant. Scope: TIER 3 disposition plus a TIER 1 typography fix.

evidence.claim: The copyright block bars any reproduction of the whole publication without the author's written permission and carves out no exception for the mechanics that the rest of the book licenses away.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: No part of this publication may be reproduced

evidence.claim: The license chapter grants the OGL terms over all rules and procedures in Chapters 1 through 22, so a reader-facing blanket bar in ch00 contradicts the book's own grant and must be reconciled before publication.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: may only be Used under and in terms of

evidence.claim: Scope framing: the carve-out wording is a legal/design-authority question (TIER 3, cross-chapter reconciliation vs ch23), while the ASCII '(c)' glyph at 00-front-matter.qmd:20 instead of the real copyright symbol is a chapter-local TIER 1 typography fix.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: TIER 3 carve-out; TIER 1 '(c)' glyph at line 20

evidence.claim: Weighing the rest of the chapter: the TBD placeholders are acceptable in this draft build, the cover-art placeholder is a committed asset with a correct caption, zero em-dashes appear in any chapter, and the ch01b title matches the brief; none of these block the disposition.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: placeholders acceptable; em-dash scan returned zero matches

payload.argument: Line 22 bans any reproduction without consent, yet ch23 line 78 licenses copying of every rule table under OGL 1.0a, and OGL section 2 (ch23 line 19) forbids extra terms. Add an OGC carve-out; Tier 3.

evidence.claim: The copyright block at line 20 reserves all rights, and line 22 bars copying or distributing the book without written consent, with no exception for licensed game content.
The OGC declaration at line 78 covers every rule table and numeric value from Chapters 1 through 22, inviting readers to copy that material under the OGL.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: all associated tables and numerical values

evidence.claim: OGL section 2, quoted at line 19, prohibits attaching any additional terms or conditions to OGC, making the blanket no-copy clause an impermissible extra restriction.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: No other terms or conditions may be applied

payload.argument: [00-front-matter.qmd:20-22] Year range matches ch23 and the cover asset is a committed valid PNG, but the blanket all-rights-reserved block omits the OGC carve-out ch23 grants.

evidence.claim: The front-matter copyright block is a blanket no-reproduction notice with no open game content carve-out [00-front-matter.qmd:22].
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: No part of this publication may be reproduced

evidence.claim: The front-matter copyright year range and holder match the ch23 copyright notice, both 2024-2026 Bruce A. Moser [00-front-matter.qmd:20 vs 23-license.qmd:51].
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: (c) 2024-2026 Bruce A. Moser. All rights reserved.

evidence.claim: ch23 designates all mechanics in Chapters 1 through 22 as open game content usable only under OGL 1.0a [23-license.qmd:76-78].
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: All game mechanics, rules systems, and procedures described in

evidence.claim: The OGL grant is a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use the mechanics, which a no-reproduction front-matter line contradicts [23-license.qmd:23].
Cover-art asset at line 32 is a real committed file: valid PNG, 1308x1693, matching the caption, last touched in commit 894e4b9, working tree clean.

payload.argument: The front matter is title page, copyright block, credits, and dedication only. A full numeric and vocabulary sweep of 00-front-matter.qmd finds no damage row, card cost, level gate, class name, or core-roll remnant; the mechanics stand clean as written.

evidence.claim: The file's only digits are the software version tag [file:5], the copyright year span [file:20], an image caption number [file:34], two pixel dimensions [file:34], and a layout width [file:32]; none is a game value.
A mechanism-vocabulary sweep for damage, prereq, card cost, level gate, 3d6, tier bounds, the nine class names, and spell terms returns no hits in the chapter.

Cross-checked the digit inventory against the locked numbers (flat 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21 damage; 2/4/8 costs; L3/L7 gates; 3d6 core roll; 9-class roster) and found zero overlap, so no budget, cost, or gate is violated.

payload.argument: 00-front-matter.qmd:50 splices a verbless 'every player' fragment into a new clause by comma; reword it (Tier 1). Nits: :9 omits the colon its siblings carry; :20 spells (c) for the symbol.

evidence.claim: At line 50 the closing sentence strands 'every player' inside a relative clause that never receives a verb, then a comma butts in a new independent clause, producing a comma splice in the book's warm voice.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: instead?", you're why this book exists.

evidence.claim: Title-page credit lines 11-16 all put a colon inside the italic label, but line 9's 'Written by' label omits it, so the block's punctuation is inconsistent.
The copyright notice at line 20 prints the letters '(c)' rather than the copyright symbol; brief scope includes the symbol in fixed-prose typography.

Fix: give the subject its own verb, e.g. close the line with 'instead?" is why this book exists.'; no dash needed since the book bans them. Also add a colon after 'Written by' and swap (c) for the symbol.

payload.argument: Title page is structurally complete: name, edition, version, author, copyright, ISBN, printing, credits and dedication all present; the two H2 sections sit at the right level and order; the TOC is build-generated, so nothing is missing.

evidence.claim: Every standard front-matter element appears in conventional order: name and edition at top, author and team credits next, legal notice, then identifier and printing lines, before the sectioned credits and closing page.
This file is pulled into the book's opening chapter with no H1 of its own, so the two level-2 headings are the correct depth for its subsections.
The book format produces the contents listing at build time to this heading depth, so a manual contents pointer inside the front matter would be redundant.
A reader landing on the title page needs no how-to-use note here, because the first chapter opens by explaining the game loop in plain terms.

payload.argument: Build output splits the framed title block across pages 9-10: rule [00-front-matter.qmd:18] lands atop a ~85% empty page 10 with the legal block stranded below it, and the title line duplicates the chapter ornament on page 9 [00-front-matter.qmd:2].

evidence.claim: PDF p.9 ends with the credits block at ~y=715 of 792pt, i.e. flush with the bottom margin, so the second rule plus the (c) and rights lines have no room and flow to p.10; p.10 then shows only the diamond rule at y~80 and six short lines, with no ink below y~250 (75%+ of the page empty).
The two rules at lines 7 and 18 are meant to frame one continuous title block (title, credits, legal notice), but the build breaks that unit between the credits and the legal notice.

The bold title and edition line at 00-front-matter.qmd:2-3 restate, word for word, the book title and subtitle already displayed by the chapter ornament higher on the same page (y~222-299 vs y~550-587).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Heroes of Legend Core Rules, First Edition

evidence.claim: The notice line at 00-front-matter.qmd:20 renders as literal (c) text, while the same pages use real typographic glyphs elsewhere (diamond ornament, multiplication sign), so the copyright sign reads as untypeset ASCII.

dissent.position: supported - a full numeric and vocabulary sweep finds no damage row, card cost, level gate, class name, or core-roll remnant in the front matter; the mechanics stand clean as written, so the refute is driven by the legal/typography items, not by any mechanic.

supported - the title page is structurally complete with all standard front-matter elements in conventional order, the two H2 sections sit at the correct depth for an included file, and the contents listing is build-generated, so nothing is missing; the refute is driven by the legal carve-out and typography, not by completeness.

payload.rationale: topic t-01 is rejected by a 5-2 refute majority with no rebuttals and no impasse, so it closes rejected and the librarian synthesizes the tiered disposition. The load-bearing finding, independently confirmed across librarian/contrarian/researcher, is that the front-matter copyright notice (line 22) is a blanket no-reproduction bar with no carve-out, directly contradicting ch23's OGC designation (line 78) that licenses all game mechanics under OGL 1.0a, which OGL section 2 (ch23 line 19) makes a perpetual royalty-free grant and forbids extra terms on. That is a legal/design-authority question (TIER 3) because the carve-out wording is the book's legal face. The typography, punctuation, comma-splice, and duplicate-title items are chapter-local with no content judgment (TIER 1), verified against the built PDF (printed p.9-10) and the source. The year-range and asset checks (TIER 2) are canon-determined and already match, so they close with verification only.
payload.recommendation: VERDICT: REJECTED 5-2. Five voters (librarian, contrarian, researcher, author, layout-expert) refuted topic t-01, two (game-architect, editor-in-chief) supported, none rebutted, no impasse, no judge sat. ch00 (quarto-book/chapters/00-front-matter.qmd) does not publish as written: its blanket all-rights-reserved copyright notice carries no exception for the game mechanics the book licenses away under the OGL. Execute this TIERED DISPOSITION PLAN, built on dispositions I independently verified against the book chapters and the built PDF (source of record). TIER 1 (mechanical, chapter-local, no mechanics change, no content judgment) - ship as one micro-PR on quarto-book/chapters/00-front-matter.qmd only: (1) Replace the ASCII '(c)' at line 20 with the real copyright glyph U+00A9 so the notice renders typeset, matching the real typographic glyphs elsewhere in the front matter. (2) Add the colon the other five credit labels carry, so line 9 reads 'Written by:' not 'Written by'. (3) Repair the comma splice at line 50 in the Special Thanks closing sentence, which strands the subject 'every player' in a relative clause that never receives a verb before a comma butts in the new clause 'you're why this book exists'; give the subject its own verb (close with 'instead?' is why this book exists) with no em-dash. (4) Remove the explicit title block at lines 2-3 (the bold 'Heroes of Legend' and 'Core Rules, First Edition'): the front matter is included inside Chapter I, and index.qmd already sets the book title and subtitle that the chapter ornament renders higher on the same page, so the block is word-for-word duplicate (verified in the built PDF, printed p.9). TIER 3 (legal/design-authority, implement the recommended default anchored on OGL 1.0a standard practice and log each in decisions-pending.md as 'implemented default 2026-09-03, veto to revert'): (5) Add an Open Game Content carve-out to the copyright block so it no longer flatly contradicts ch23. ch23 line 78 designates all game mechanics, rules systems, and procedures in Chapters 1 through 22 as Open Game Content usable only under OGL 1.0a, and OGL section 2 (ch23 line 19) forbids attaching additional terms to OGC; the front-matter blanket no-reproduction notice (line 22) is exactly such an extra restriction. Add a sentence stating the game mechanics are Open Game Content governed by the OGL in Chapter 23, with all other material remaining all-rights-reserved. TIER 2 (substantive / cross-chapter reconciliation): (6) Verify the copyright year range and holder against ch23 (both '2024-2026 Bruce A. Moser', confirmed matching) and confirm the cover-art asset at line 32 is a committed valid PNG (1308x1693, matches caption, commit 894e4b9, clean tree - confirmed). No further action beyond the TIER 1 fixes. game-architect and editor-in-chief found the mechanics and structure sound as written, so no TIER 2 rewrite is required.

resolved.outcome: rejected 5-2 - chapter does not publish as written; execute the tiered disposition plan (4 TIER 1 chapter-local fixes in one micro-PR, 1 TIER 3 OGC carve-out implemented as default and logged in decisions-pending.md, 1 TIER 2 cross-chapter reconciliation closed on verification)
